findings.section: Choose it or not: Amazon S3 or Amazon EBS or Amazon EFS
findings.quote: | File storage, through [industry-standard protocols like NFS and SMB](../facts/s3.md#s3-vs-file-storage-shared-mount) |
findings.evidence: Fact s3-vs-file-storage-shared-mount has scope "file-based storage, compared with object and block storage"; its quote is about file storage in general ("File-based storage is natively mountable ... using industry-standard protocols like NFS and SMB"), not about Amazon EFS. Under the column header "Amazon EFS" the cell tells her that EFS speaks SMB. On the exam, SMB is the signal for Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, not EFS (FREQUENCY.md: "EFS vs FSx Windows vs Lustre vs ONTAP | Linux NFS vs SMB/AD/DFS"), and her diagnostic lists EFS vs FSx as right-but-unsure. Fix: rename the column "File storage (Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx)", or link an EFS fact that names NFS only and leave SMB to chapter 23.
findings.resolution: fix-21: the column header is now "File storage (Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx)", so NFS and SMB are not attributed to Amazon EFS alone; SMB is left to chapter 23.

findings.section: Every new object is encrypted with SSE-S3 unless you choose another key
findings.quote: | SSE-C | You, in every request | S3 encrypts, but keys stay outside AWS |
findings.evidence: Fact s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04 (verified, checked 2026-10-12): "Starting April 2026, SSE-C is disabled by default for all new general purpose buckets and existing buckets in accounts with no SSE-C encrypted objects." and "If your workload requires SSE-C, you must explicitly enable it by setting `BlockedEncryptionTypes` to `NONE` in your bucket's default encryption configuration using the `PutBucketEncryption` API." RULINGS hard rule 7 requires a Changed recently note for a change since mid-2022. The chapter teaches SSE-C as a ready answer (1-fast signals row, 2-deep Exam signal, card s3-c006, q010 twin) and never says that a new bucket now rejects SSE-C writes until it is enabled. She works at AWS and will advise customers on this. Fix: a Changed recently box (old: any bucket accepts SSE-C requests; now: blocked by default from April 2026; the exam probably expects the old behavior) and one line in this subsection.
findings.resolution: fix-21: same fix as claims technical-03: Changed recently entry (2026-04) in 1-fast.md, one line in the encryption subsection, card s3-c006.

findings.quote: | "AWS must never store the encryption keys" | server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C), or client-side encryption | with SSE-C, [you retain control of the encryption keys](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-sse-c-keys) | AWS services read the objects: keys in AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) |
findings.evidence: The row gives two answers for one signal, while the official sample question (FREQUENCY.md: "SSE-C or client-side encryption when keys stay on-premises") and the twins q006/q010 decide between them by one phrase: "Amazon S3 itself must encrypt" points to SSE-C, "encrypted before it leaves the data center" points to client-side encryption (fact s3-client-side-encryption-not-exposed-to-aws: "aren't exposed to any third party, including AWS"). The guard names a case (keys in AWS KMS) that contradicts the stem phrase it guards. STYLE rule 9: "But not if" names the alternative. Fix: Think = SSE-C; But not if = "AWS must never see unencrypted data: client-side encryption".
findings.resolution: fix-21: Think = SSE-C only; But not if = "data is encrypted before it leaves the data center: client-side encryption".

findings.section: Choose it or not: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval or Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive
findings.quote: | How long does a read take? | [Milliseconds](../facts/s3.md#s3-class-glacier-ir-compare-row) | [Minutes to 12 hours](../facts/s3.md#s3-class-glacier-flexible-compare-row) | [9 to 48 hours](../facts/s3.md#s3-class-deep-archive-compare-row) |
findings.evidence: s3-class-deep-archive-compare-row is the "Average retrieval times" column ("9 to 48 hours"). Ten lines later the signals table says "archive for years, retrieval within 12 hours, lowest cost" points to Deep Archive, and 2-deep.md shows Standard "[Within 12 hours](../facts/s3.md#s3-archive-retrieval-times-deep)". A reader who compares "9 to 48 hours" with a "within 12 hours" stem rejects Deep Archive, which is the answer (q007, FREQUENCY.md "12-48 h -> Deep Archive"). Fix: show the options in the fast table ("Standard within 12 hours, Bulk within 48 hours" from s3-archive-retrieval-times-deep), or label the cell "average" and add the 12-hour Standard value.
findings.resolution: fix-21: the Deep Archive cell now shows "Standard: within 12 hours" (s3-archive-retrieval-times-deep) instead of the 9 to 48 hours average, matching the signal row and the restore table.

findings.quote: objects are [smaller than 1 GB](../facts/s3.md#s3-transfer-acceleration-vs-cloudfront-small-objects): CloudFront PUT and POST
findings.evidence: Fact s3-transfer-acceleration-vs-cloudfront-small-objects says only "you should consider using Amazon CloudFront's PUT/POST commands": advice, not a decision rule. Exam stems about slow long-distance uploads to one bucket point to Transfer Acceleration whatever the size; the reported decision is "S3 Transfer Acceleration vs CloudFront vs multipart | Long-distance uploads vs global downloads vs large objects" (FREQUENCY.md). The guard teaches her to reject the right answer for a 500 MB upload stem. The same guard is the q019 twin ("If the stem said \"files smaller than 1 GB\" instead: consider CloudFront PUT/POST"). Fix: guard "the same files are downloaded by users worldwide: CloudFront" or "one large file fails midway: multipart upload"; change the q019 twin the same way.
findings.resolution: fix-21: the 1-fast guard is now "users around the world download the same files: CloudFront". The q019 twin text was not edited: an edit of a verified question resets its verification (R5), and that text restates AWS guidance from a verified fact ("consider CloudFront PUT/POST").

findings.quote: a role signs it: the URL [expires when the role session ends](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-expires-with-temporary-credentials)
findings.evidence: STYLE rule 9: "But not if" names the alternative. This guard is a caveat; the answer stays a presigned URL. The decision the exam asks is "S3 presigned URL vs CloudFront signed URL vs signed cookies vs OAC | Direct S3 object vs via CDN vs many files" (FREQUENCY.md). Fix: "the files are served through CloudFront, or many files at once: CloudFront signed URLs or signed cookies" (xref 15).
findings.resolution: fix-21: guard now "files are served through CloudFront: CloudFront signed URLs or cookies".

findings.section: Infrequent access classes add retrieval fees and a minimum storage duration
findings.quote: A common belief is that S3 Standard-IA is the cheaper choice for any rarely read data. Data read [more than once a month](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-standard-vs-ia-access-frequency) belongs in S3 Standard.
findings.evidence: The truth answers a different belief: data read more than once a month is not "rarely read". The belief the distractors actually use (q021 option b, q002 option a, speak s3-s02 must_not_say "Standard-IA is always cheaper for old data") is about small objects, short-lived objects and retrieval fees: facts s3-ia-min-billable-size, s3-ia-min-duration-charge, s3-faq-standard-ia-retrieval-charge. Fix: "Truth: objects under [128 KB] are billed as 128 KB, objects deleted before [30 days] pay for 30 days, and each read pays a retrieval fee."
findings.resolution: fix-21: the trap truth now names the per-GB retrieval charge and the 128 KB minimum billable size.

findings.section: s3-q007, s3-q021, s3-q022 (status verified, not shipped)
findings.evidence: 5-quiz.md prints 18 questions; s3-q007 (core, 4.1.S9, edited-pass), s3-q021 (4.1.K7) and s3-q022 (4.1.K1) have status "verified" and are not printed. As shipped, bullets 4.1.S9 "Selecting the correct data lifecycle for storage" and 4.1.K7 "Data lifecycles" have no question, and the lifecycle subsection has only s3-q018 (cleanup). A lifecycle plan from an access pattern is the most reported S3 pattern (FREQUENCY.md rank 1: "Storage classes and minimum durations; lifecycle"). Meanwhile s3-q013 (difficulty 1, decided by the phrase "as one object") ships. Fix: ship s3-q007 and s3-q021, and cut a difficulty-1 item if the count must stay 18.
findings.resolution: fix-21: s3-q021 (4.1.K7, difficulty 3) set to ready and s3-q013 (difficulty 1) set back to verified, so 18 ship (9 core, 9 extended, 2 twin pairs, 2 multi). s3-q007 stays in the verified pool: shipping it needs a second core cut, and the only core difficulty-1 item is s3-q002 (Intelligent-Tiering, which the reader lists as unsure).

findings.evidence: Registry: 4.1.S1 is "Designing appropriate storage strategies (for example, batch uploads to Amazon S3 compared with individual uploads)"; s3-q020 tests whether an S3 event notification can target an SQS FIFO queue. 3.1.K2 is "Storage services with appropriate use cases (for example, Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS)"; s3-q013 tests multipart upload. No question asks S3 vs EBS vs EFS, although 1-fast.md has that comparison table. So 4.1.S1 and 3.1.K2 are covered only by label. Fix: a question that picks S3, EBS or EFS from the access method, and one on aggregating many small uploads (s3-q021 already fits 4.1.S1 better than 4.1.K7).
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: needs new questions (S3 vs EBS vs EFS by access method; batch uploads) and a blind-panel verification; out of scope of a fix that must not reset questions.

findings.section: A presigned URL lends the permission of its signer until the URL expires
findings.quote: 3. **Use.** The browser sends GET or PUT directly to Amazon S3.
findings.evidence: CORS is one of the 10 official sample questions (FREQUENCY.md section 1: "The official sample questions [A3] cover: ... S3 CORS"). Fact s3-cors-purpose is verified ("A browser would normally block JavaScript from allowing those requests, but with CORS you can configure your bucket to explicitly enable cross-origin requests") but appears only in a speak follow-up (speak.json s3-s01), which is not even printed. The browser-upload subsection is the natural place: a page on another domain needs a CORS configuration on the bucket. Fix: one step or Go deeper line, one signal row ("browser on another domain is blocked"), one question.
findings.resolution: fix-21: CORS line added to presigned step 3 (s3-cors-purpose). A signal row and a new question are deferred (1-fast at 1,794 of 1,800 words; a new question needs verification).

findings.section: Every new object is encrypted with SSE-S3 unless you choose another key
findings.quote: | SSE-KMS | AWS KMS | You need key permissions and an audit trail |
findings.evidence: S3 Bucket Keys are not mentioned anywhere in the chapter, though verified facts exist: s3-bucket-key-reduces-kms-requests ("enable S3 Bucket Keys to decrease request traffic from Amazon S3 to AWS KMS and reduce the cost of encryption") and s3-bucket-key-kms-cost-up-to-99-percent ("up to 99 percent"). FREQUENCY.md reports "SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS (+ bucket keys)" as a common comparison; the stem "SSE-KMS costs too much / KMS throttling" points to it (task 4.1). Fix: one row or sentence, one card, ideally one question.
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: S3 Bucket Keys need a row, a card and ideally a question; 2-deep.md is at 5,496 of 5,500 words (L201).

findings.quote: | [3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE](../facts/s3.md#s3-prefix-request-rate-baseline) | Write requests per second per prefix |
findings.evidence: Bullet 3.1.S1 "Determining storage services and configurations that meet performance demands" has no subsection on S3 request performance. The read rate of the same fact is left out (s3-prefix-request-rate-baseline: "5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned Amazon S3 prefix"), and verified facts s3-prefix-parallel-reads-55000 ("10 prefixes", "55,000 read requests per second") and s3-byte-range-fetch-parallel ("fetch different byte ranges", "higher aggregate throughput") are unused. Stems such as "reads throttle at high request rates" or "speed up downloads of large objects" have nothing to match. Fix: a short subsection or Go deeper (spread keys over prefixes, parallel byte-range GETs, multipart for writes), the GET value in the B-list, and a signal row.
findings.resolution: partly done by fix-21: the 5,500 GET/HEAD baseline row was added to the B-list and the write row now says baseline per partitioned prefix. A request-performance subsection (prefixes, byte-range GETs) is deferred: word budget.

findings.section: Intelligent-Tiering moves an unread object to cheaper tiers with no retrieval fee; Object Lock compliance mode stops every user from deleting a version until its date
findings.quote: 3. **A read.** The object is [automatically moved back to the Frequent Access tier](../facts/s3.md#s3-int-tiering-move-back), with [no retrieval fees](../facts/s3.md#s3-int-tiering-no-retrieval-fees).
findings.evidence: s3-q016 option d ("S3 Intelligent-Tiering with the Deep Archive Access tier turned on") tests the optional archive tiers, but the subsection never mentions them, and its heading and step 3 suggest every read is immediate. Fact s3-intelligent-tiering-archive-tiers-need-restore: "If the object that you are retrieving is stored in the Archive Access or Deep Archive Access tiers, first restore the object by using `RestoreObject`." Likewise the legal hold (fact s3-object-lock-retention-vs-legal-hold) appears only in speak s3-s03, not in the Object Lock subsection, although "legal hold" is a common Object Lock stem word. Fix: one Go deeper line each.
findings.resolution: fix-21: Intelligent-Tiering Why line now says objects in the two optional archive access tiers need a restore first (s3-intelligent-tiering-archive-tiers-need-restore); FAQ 6 is now the legal hold (s3-faq-object-lock-legal-hold).

findings.section: Numbers that decide answers (Changed recently box)
findings.quote: > **The exam probably expects:** the old minimum stay in S3 Standard first. Do not let this number decide an answer.
findings.evidence: Fact s3-change-lifecycle-ia-no-30-day-minimum-2026-07 (not examinable yet, GA 2026-07-16). The box says the exam expects the old 30-day stay in S3 Standard before a transition to an IA class, but the lifecycle subsection never teaches that rule, so the reader meets the old value only inside a B-list box. Exam stems with "transition to S3 Standard-IA after 7 days" depend on it. Fix: put one line in the lifecycle subsection (step 2 or 3) with the old rule and the change, and move or repeat the box there.
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: a lifecycle line with the old 30-day rule did not fit (2-deep.md at 5,496 of 5,500 words); the box under the B-list still states it.

findings.quote: "flag": "Option B says SSE-C is allowed in the bucket's default encryption settings, but SSE-C is chosen per request and is not a default-encryption option
findings.evidence: The ambiguity flag that rejected s3-q006 is itself out of date: fact s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04 says SSE-C is now allowed or blocked in "your bucket's default encryption configuration using the `PutBucketEncryption` API". With s3-q006 rejected, the SSE-C half of the official sample pair has no shipped question; s3-q010 ships with twin_of pointing at a rejected item. Fix: write a new SSE-C question under a fresh id that matches the April 2026 default, and pair it with s3-q010.
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: a new SSE-C question under a fresh id needs the blind panel; not written in a fix stage.

findings.evidence: Of the 18 shipped questions, 3 are difficulty 1 (s3-q013, s3-q019, s3-q002), 12 are difficulty 2 and 3 are difficulty 3 (s3-q017, s3-q020, s3-q018); 2 are multiple-response. Most stems carry one deciding phrase that is also in the keywords. The real exam mixes in longer stems with two constraints that pull in different directions (cost against a retrieval time, security against operational overhead). Fix: when s3-q007 and s3-q021 ship (finding 21-exam-08), drop a difficulty-1 item.
findings.resolution: fix-21: one difficulty-1 item (s3-q013) swapped out for a difficulty-3 lifecycle item (s3-q021); see 21-exam-08.
